question: A charity's volunteering team is deciding whether to hand its volunteer reference-checking process over to Claude. In which order should these steps be taken?
options: A) Work out which parts of the process a mistake would make hard to undo; run the resulting arrangement on a small batch of references; keep those parts with staff and give Claude only the rest; widen it to the full caseload once that batch holds up.

B) Keep those parts with staff and give Claude only the rest; work out which parts of the process a mistake would make hard to undo; run the resulting arrangement on a small batch of references; widen it to the full caseload once that batch holds up.

C) Work out which parts of the process a mistake would make hard to undo; keep those parts with staff and give Claude only the rest; run the resulting arrangement on a small batch of references; widen it to the full caseload once that batch holds up.

D) Run the resulting arrangement on a small batch of references; work out which parts of the process a mistake would make hard to undo; keep those parts with staff and give Claude only the rest; widen it to the full caseload once that batch holds up.
correct_answers: C) Work out which parts of the process a mistake would make hard to undo; keep those parts with staff and give Claude only the rest; run the resulting arrangement on a small batch of references; widen it to the full caseload once that batch holds up.
explanations: The risky steps are identified but the pilot begins before they have been kept with staff, so the small batch is run through exactly the arrangement the assessment warned against.
The split between staff and Claude is made before anyone has judged where an error would be irreversible, so the assessment that should have produced the split arrives after it.

Correct. Reversibility is what decides which steps may be delegated, so it is assessed before anything is handed over; the split follows from that assessment; the arrangement is then proved on a small batch where a mistake is contained; and only evidence from that batch justifies the full caseload.
The pilot runs before the process has been divided at all, which means the batch tests an undefined arrangement and real volunteer references are handled with no safeguard in place.
